A circuit breaker is a safety feature in electrical circuits that helps prevent overloads and prevents damage to the system. It works by temporarily stopping power to a circuit when it detects a problem, such as a short circuit or a fault in the wiring. This prevents the circuit from overheating or causing a complete failure, which could lead to fires, equipment damage, or even power outages.

When a circuit breaker trips, it stops the power supply to the affected circuit, allowing other circuits to operate normally. This helps protect the system from damage and ensures that power is available to other devices and equipment.
